requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.ci.span` is satisfied. The implementation is complete and marked, and the tests cover the obligations and their boundaries.

**Implementation**
- `colon_fence` (src/lib.rs:666) accepts a line only if it has at most three leading spaces and at least three colons. A line indented by four or more spaces is not a fence. This is marked `{impl}`.
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs:522) requires the text after the colons to start with `{req}`, then whitespace, then a valid name.
  - A missing space (`:::{req}ready`) is rejected.
  - An opening fence inside a Markdown code block is ignored.
- The same function finds the closing fence as the first later line, outside code blocks, that satisfies both conditions below. This matches "at least as many colons, nothing else except whitespace".
  - Its colon count is at least that of the opening fence.
  - Nothing but whitespace follows the colons.
- A line such as `:::foo` does not close the block.
- The body runs from the end of the opening line to the start of the closing line. This covers headings, nested directives, code and blank lines, and nothing after the closing fence is included. The block's `end` is the end of the closing line, so following text is excluded.
- `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:359, marked `{impl}` at the body computation) builds the text with `without_options(...).trim()`. This excludes leading and trailing whitespace. Stripping option lines is the job of `requirements.references.anchors`, not this requirement.
- A missing closing fence is reported as an error.
- The other users of `definition_blocks` (`preprocess_book`, `replace_definitions`, `marker_ranges`, `direct_references`) reuse the same parser. They implement other requirements and do not add unmarked span behaviour.

**Tests** (all marked `{test}` for `requirements.ci.span`)
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` (src/lib.rs:1276) checks:
  - `:::foo` does not close the block, but `::: ` with trailing whitespace does.
  - Three-space indentation works for both opening and closing fences.
  - A four-space-indented opener is not a definition.
  - A four-space-indented closer leaves the block unclosed.
  - `:::{req}ready` is rejected.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` (src/lib.rs:1260) checks the body of a four-colon fence containing a three-colon directive, and that text after the closer is outside the block.
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` (src/evidence.rs:2395) checks a body with a fenced code block containing `:::`, ATX and Setext headings, and a following requirement and outside text. The recorded body must equal the exact span.
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` (src/evidence.rs:2298) checks whitespace trimming.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (src/evidence.rs:1749) is a positive end-to-end case.
- `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` (src/evidence.rs:2428) checks the unclosed-fence error.
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` (src/evidence.rs:2461) is marked only for `fence_lengths`, but it also exercises longer closers.

No acknowledged gaps (FIXMEs) were found, and I found no unmarked implementation of this requirement.
